title: Lexique
covers: Meeting; Réunion; Musique; Nez au vent; Leader; Train
note: France Galop distinguishes Meeting (a series of réunions at one racecourse over a period) from Réunion (races at one racecourse on one day); this blocks a universal Meeting=Race meeting merge.

title: British Horseracing Authority publishes 2027 fixture list
note: BHA states 1,440 fixtures are scheduled for 2027 and treats Fixture as a scheduled unit in the official fixture list.

title: IABRW Article 1 — Recognition and Categorization of Quality Races
note: IFHA presents Group and Grade as corresponding quality-race descriptions across racing authorities; use regional_counterpart rather than global exact-synonym identity.

title: Racing statistics — Race off-times data
covers: actual race off-times; scheduled off time; punctuality
note: BHA publishes actual race off-time performance and defines late races by comparison with scheduled off time, proving these are distinct time concepts.

title: Ensuring more races start on time: a modified approach for 2025
covers: scheduled off time; race start punctuality
note: BHA explicitly uses scheduled off time as the pre-announced start-time trigger and discusses races going off on time relative to it.

title: Racing 101 — Track Ratings
covers: Track Ratings; racetrack condition; Firm 1 through Heavy 10
note: Racing Victoria defines Track Ratings as an official measure of racetrack conditions; this supports a regional Track condition system distinct from GB Going terminology.

title: Track Information
covers: Track as race venue/listing entity; address; racing dates; track size
note: USTA's current Track Information page uses Track for venue/listing entities with addresses, dates and codes, demonstrating a facility-level Track sense distinct from physical-surface usage in racing rules.

title: Racing Terms — Layoff
note: Industry education describes Layoff as an extended break/time away from racing; use with authority-published Australia/NZ Spell evidence to model Spell as a narrower regional recuperative-break concept.
